subject: biology-1
question: In addition to helping harvest light, carotenoids protect the photosynthetic machinery from damage. Which of the following best describes that protective role?

options.text: They convert excess light energy into extra ATP that speeds up the Calvin cycle.
They absorb excess light energy and dissipate it as heat, protecting chlorophyll from damage.
They absorb only green light, which the plant safely discards as waste.
They reflect all incoming light away from the leaf so the pigments stay cool.

explanation: Carotenoids are accessory pigments that absorb excess light energy and harmlessly release it as heat, shielding chlorophyll from photo-oxidative damage. A gets the mechanism backwards, because excess light energy is not converted into useful ATP. C is wrong because carotenoids absorb blue-green light rather than green light. D describes reflection, which would steal energy from photosynthesis instead of protecting it.
